### Gin API reference, generated by Sourcey

Path: `/gin-sourcey-docs/introduction/`

A Sourcey-generated documentation site for github.com/gin-gonic/gin at a pinned commit.

This site is a Sourcey-generated documentation site for a maintained third-party open-source library : github.com/gin-gonic/gin , the Go HTTP web framework, at a pinned public commit . Fact Value Target repository https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin Pinned commit 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 Commit date 2026-10-10T12:20:35+08:00 ( docs: include HTTP QUERY method in RouterGroup.Any (#4879) ) License MIT ( Copyright (c) 2014-present Manuel Martínez-Almeida ) Module path github.com/gin-gonic/gin ( go 1.26.0 ) Files in the pinned tree 130 tracked files, 99 .go files Documented packages 7 Documented public API entries 431 (59 types, 62 functions, 237 methods, 47 constants, 26 variables) Source files contributing to the reference 53 Docs engine Sourcey v3.6.12 ( sourcey npm package, AGPL-3.0) Go toolchain used for the snapshot go version go1.26.0 linux/amd64 Snapshot artifact godoc.json (Sourcey godoc snapshot, schema_version: 1 ), sha256 91bfb81dff5fafadf8ea973ee99da82eb5bf0c82d0e0e854ea7e0a88bb070e15 What was actually run Nothing on this site was hand-written from memory. The Go reference tab is rendered from a godoc snapshot taken from the pinned clone of the target repository : Copy git clone https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin.git # at 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 sourcey godoc -m . -p ./... -o godoc.json # Sourcey v3.6.12, Go 1.26.0 sourcey build # renders the site from sourcey.config.ts Every symbol on the Go API tab carries the doc comment, the source-faithful declaration and the source position ( file:line ) that Sourcey extracted from that commit. See reproduce for the exact commands and digests, coverage for what is documented, and gaps for the maintainer-facing findings. Why an ecosystem audience would link this gin is one of the most used Go HTTP frameworks: its public surface ( gin.Engine , gin.RouterGroup , gin.Context , the binding and render packages) is what application code calls, and it is the part of the codebase that changes most often. A godoc-style reference for a specific commit is what a maintainer needs when a released version and main disagree, and what a downstream team needs when a dependency is pinned in a lockfile and the upstream docs have already moved on. This site answers that question for one pinned commit, from the source of that commit, with nothing hand-maintained in between. Disclosure The docs were generated by an AI agent (the SPORE crew) using the open-source Sourcey engine. The reference content is machine-extracted from the MIT-licensed gin source tree; the guide pages (this one, coverage, gaps, reproduce) were written by the crew and are marked as such in the report.

The 20+ entry points a reader lands on first These are the exported symbols a Go developer touches on day one, all present in the Go API tab with their source positions: gin.New() — create an *gin.Engine gin.Default() — engine with the Logger and Recovery middleware attached (*gin.Engine).Run(addr string) error (*gin.Engine).Use(middleware ...HandlerFunc) IRoutes (*gin.Engine).GET(path string, handlers ...HandlerFunc) IRoutes (*gin.Engine).POST(path string, handlers ...HandlerFunc) IRoutes (*gin.Engine).Group(relativePath string, handlers ...HandlerFunc) *RouterGroup (*gin.RouterGroup).Group(relativePath string, handlers ...HandlerFunc) *RouterGroup (*gin.RouterGroup).StaticFS(relativePath string, fs http.FileSystem) IRoutes (*gin.Engine).ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) (*gin.Context).Param(key string) string (*gin.Context).Query(key string) string (*gin.Context).JSON(code int, obj any) (*gin.Context).BindJSON(obj any) error (*gin.Context).ShouldBindJSON(obj any) error (*gin.Context).Get(key string) (any, bool) (*gin.Context).Set(key string, value any) (*gin.Context).Next() (*gin.Context).AbortWithStatus(code int) (*gin.Context).Redirect(code int, location string) gin.HandlerFunc — the middleware type every extension point takes gin.H — the map type used for JSON responses gin.Error and (*gin.Error).Error() string binding.Bind , binding.BindJSON , binding.BindQuery , binding.Validator render.Render — the response renderer interface implemented by every renderer Deliberate omissions Unexported symbols are excluded ( includeUnexported: false , the default). They are implementation detail and are not part of the public contract. internal/ packages are included only where go list ./... resolves them as buildable packages ( internal/bytesconv , internal/fs ). Their exported names are not importable by third parties and are documented for completeness only. Examples : the pinned gin tree contains no func Example... functions ( grep '^func Example' **/*.go returns nothing), so the snapshot legitimately carries zero runnable examples. This is a property of the library at this commit, not a gap in the extraction. Non-Go assets (benchmarks, docs/ , CI configuration) are out of scope for a godoc surface and are not documented here.

### Maintainer-facing gaps

Path: `/gin-sourcey-docs/gaps/`

What a maintainer of github.com/gin-gonic/gin would want to know after reading the pinned commit's public surface.

These are findings from reading the pinned commit ( 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 ) through the generated reference — not a summary of what pages exist. Each one names a file and line in the pinned tree so it can be checked in one click. 1. The new QUERY method is documented in code but nowhere else The pinned commit is itself the QUERY support change ( docs: include HTTP QUERY method in RouterGroup.Any (#4879) ). The code side is good: routergroup.go:14-17 declares the shim, routergroup.go:176 adds (*RouterGroup).QUERY , and routergroup.go:181 lists QUERY in Any 's doc comment. The README never mentions it : grep -ic query README.md returns 0 at this commit. A reader who learns about RFC 10008 QUERY support from the godoc reference has no path from the README to it, and the README's route tables are the place a Go developer actually looks. Adding the method to the README's routing section (and to the Any list there, if the README has one) is a small, high-value change. 2. MethodQuery is a hand-rolled shim that will need a migration plan Copy // routergroup.go:14-17 // MethodQuery is the HTTP QUERY method defined by RFC 10008. It is declared // here because the standard library does not provide http.MethodQuery yet. const MethodQuery = "QUERY" The constant is correct today, but it is a duplicate of a stdlib symbol the comment itself predicts will arrive . When the standard library ships http.MethodQuery , this shim becomes a second source of truth for the same method name, and the two can drift (for example if the stdlib spelling or the net/http method table changes). A maintainer note pointing at the upstream Go issue ( golang/go#71459 tracks the QUERY method proposal) with a planned migration step would turn a silent future conflict into a scheduled one. 3. Four exported entry points have no doc comment at all Measured over the 431 exported entries in the snapshot, exactly four have an empty doc comment: Symbol Location Why it matters type ContextKeyType int context.go:52 It is the type of the exported ContextRequestKey constant ( context.go:54 ) and the type behind the documented ContextKey ("_gin-gonic/gin/contextkey", context.go:50 ). The doc comment stops one line short of the type it describes. (*gin.Engine).Handler gin.go:257 It is the http.Handler adapter for the engine (and the H2C path). It is the method a Go server integration needs, and it is the only public method on Engine with no comment. type SliceValidationError []error binding/default_validator.go:21 It is the error type returned by multi-field validation. Users must type-assert on it to report which field failed, and the doc comment exists only on its Error() method, not on the type. binding.MapFormWithTag binding/form_mapping.go:40 The exported, tag-aware form binder. Its unexported sibling mapForm ( binding/form_mapping.go:36 ) is the same function with a fixed tag; the exported one has no comment, so the tag semantics ( form , json , …) and the pointer requirements are undiscoverable. For a framework whose binding package is a stable extension point, that last one is the costly omission: it is exported precisely so that users can call it. 4. (*gin.Context).BindWith is deprecated but still exported and documented deprecated.go:17 still ships BindWith , which logs a deprecation warning on every call and then delegates to MustBindWith . The doc comment says "Deprecated: Use MustBindWith or ShouldBindWith", which is correct, but the symbol is still part of the public surface at this commit and will still show up in the generated reference. A maintainer note about the removal horizon (the linked upstream issue is #662) would let downstream code plan the migration. 5. ginS is a global-singleton package with wrapper-only documentation The ginS package (26 exported functions) wraps a single process-global engine created with sync.OnceValue ( ginS/gins.go:16-18 ). Every exported function is documented as "is a wrapper for Engine.X" — e.g. LoadHTMLGlob , SetMode , Run , Secure , LoadHTMLFiles . Two maintainer-facing consequences: The doc text describes the delegate , not the semantics of sharing one engine process-wide — the part a user needs before choosing the package. The package is not in the module's public README surface, so the reference page is the only place its behaviour is described. 6. The render package's public surface is larger than its documentation render contributes 23 types, 3 functions and 38 methods from 14 files — the second-largest contributor in the snapshot. Its per-renderer docs are consistent ( Render implements render.Render ), but the package-level relationship between render.Render , render.Render interface implementations and the Context.Render dispatch table is only discoverable by reading context.go . A maintainer-facing "which renderer do I use for X" map would remove the need to read the dispatch code. How these were found Every finding above was read out of the same snapshot that renders this site: positions ( file:line ) come from Sourcey's godoc extraction, the "no doc comment" set is the set of exported entries with an empty doc string in godoc.json , and the README claim is a case-insensitive grep over the pinned README.md at that commit (0 matches). Re-running the extraction on a later commit re-measures all of them.

### Reproduce

Path: `/gin-sourcey-docs/reproduce/`

The exact commands and digests that produce this site from the pinned gin commit.

Every artifact on this site is re-creatable from the pinned commit with the commands below. Nothing is hand-transcribed. 0. Toolchain Copy node --version # v22.14.0 npm --version # 10.9.2 go version # go version go1.26.0 linux/amd64 npx sourcey --version # sourcey v3.6.12 runx --version # runx-cli 0.10.2 The go toolchain reports go1.26.0 because gin 's go.mod declares go 1.26.0 and the Go toolchain switches automatically to satisfy it ( GOTOOLCHAIN=auto ). 1. Pin the target Copy git clone https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin.git gin cd gin git checkout 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 git rev-parse HEAD # 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 2. Take the godoc snapshot from that source Copy sourcey godoc -m . -p ./... -o godoc.json Output (Sourcey v3.6.12): Copy Sourcey: wrote godoc snapshot for github.com/gin-gonic/gin Packages: 7 Output: godoc.json Digest of the committed snapshot: Copy sha256sum godoc.json # 91bfb81dff5fafadf8ea973ee99da82eb5bf0c82d0e0e854ea7e0a88bb070e15 The snapshot is a runx / sourcey godoc snapshot , schema_version: 1 , with module_path: github.com/gin-gonic/gin and generated_at recorded in the file. It is committed to this repository so the site can be rebuilt on a JS-only host with no Go toolchain, which is the workflow Sourcey documents for godoc tabs. 3. Build the site Copy sourcey build sourcey.config.ts in this repository renders two tabs: Guides — the markdown pages in this repository ( introduction.md , coverage.md , gaps.md , reproduce.md ); Go API — godoc({ module: "./gin-src", packages: ["./..."], mode: "snapshot", snapshot: "./godoc.json", includeTests: true }) . mode: "snapshot" is deliberate: the published build must be byte-stable and rebuildable without a Go toolchain. The live path was verified separately on the build host with mode: "auto" , which re-runs go list + go/parser + go/doc against the pinned clone and produces the same 7 packages. 4. Verify the published site Copy curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://asporeteam.github.io/gin-sourcey-docs/ curl -sS https://asporeteam.github.io/gin-sourcey-docs/go/ | grep -c "gin-gonic" The published site is the dist/ output of step 3, committed to the main branch of ASporeTeam/gin-sourcey-docs and served by GitHub Pages. 5. Re-measure the findings on the gaps page Copy # the four undocumented exported entries python3 - 'PY' import json d = json.load(open("godoc.json")) for p in d["packages"]: for t in p.get("types", []): if not t.get("doc", "").strip(): pos = t.get("position") or {} print("type", t["name"], pos.get("file"), pos.get("line")) for m in t.get("methods", []): if not m.get("doc", "").strip(): pos = m.get("position") or {} print("method", t["name"] + "." + m["name"], pos.get("file"), pos.get("line")) for f in p.get("funcs", []): if not f.get("doc", "").strip(): pos = f.get("position") or {} print("func", f["name"], pos.get("file"), pos.get("line")) PY # the README never mentions the QUERY method at this commit grep -ic query README.md # 0

If it is it will then try to parse the headers defined in Engine.RemoteIPHeaders (defaulting to [X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP]). If the headers are not syntactically valid OR the remote IP does not correspond to a trusted proxy, the remote IP (coming from Request.RemoteAddr) is returned. func ContentType() string Source: context.go:1058 ContentType returns the Content-Type header of the request. func Cookie(name string) (string, error) Source: context.go:1191 Cookie returns the named cookie provided in the request or ErrNoCookie if not found. Create an instance of Engine, by using New() or Default() Copy type Engine struct { RouterGroup // RedirectTrailingSlash enables automatic redirection if the current route can't be matched but a // handler for the path with (without) the trailing slash exists. // For example if /foo/ is requested but a route only exists for /foo, the // client is redirected to /foo with http status code 301 for GET requests // and 307 for all other request methods. RedirectTrailingSlash bool // RedirectFixedPath if enabled, the router tries to fix the current request path, if no // handle is registered for it. // First superfluous path elements like ../ or // are removed. // Afterwards the router does a case-insensitive lookup of the cleaned path. // If a handle can be found for this route, the router makes a redirection // to the corrected path with status code 301 for GET requests and 307 for // all other request methods. // For example /FOO and /..//Foo could be redirected to /foo. // RedirectTrailingSlash is independent of this option. RedirectFixedPath bool // HandleMethodNotAllowed if enabled, the router checks if another method is allowed for the // current route, if the current request can not be routed. // If this is the case, the request is answered with 'Method Not Allowed' // and HTTP status code 405. // If no other Method is allowed, the request is delegated to the NotFound // handler. HandleMethodNotAllowed bool // ForwardedByClientIP if enabled, client IP will be parsed from the request's headers that // match those stored at `(*gin.Engine).RemoteIPHeaders`. If no IP was // fetched, it falls back to the IP obtained from // `(*gin.Context).Request.RemoteAddr`. ForwardedByClientIP bool // AppEngine was deprecated. // Deprecated: USE `TrustedPlatform` WITH VALUE `gin.PlatformGoogleAppEngine` INSTEAD // #726 #755 If enabled, it will trust some headers starting with // 'X-AppEngine...' for better integration with that PaaS. AppEngine bool // UseRawPath if enabled, the url.RawPath will be used to find parameters. // The RawPath is only a hint, EscapedPath() should be use instead. (https://pkg.go.dev/net/url@master#URL) // Only use RawPath if you know what you are doing. UseRawPath bool // UseEscapedPath if enable, the url.EscapedPath() will be used to find parameters // It overrides UseRawPath UseEscapedPath bool // UnescapePathValues if true, the path value will be unescaped. // If UseRawPath and UseEscapedPath are false (by default), the UnescapePathValues effectively is true, // as url.Path gonna be used, which is already unescaped. UnescapePathValues bool // RemoveExtraSlash a parameter can be parsed from the URL even with extra slashes. // See the PR #1817 and issue #1644 RemoveExtraSlash bool // RemoteIPHeaders list of headers used to obtain the client IP when // `(*gin.Engine).ForwardedByClientIP` is `true` and // `(*gin.Context).Request.RemoteAddr` is matched by at least one of the // network origins of list defined by `(*gin.Engine).SetTrustedProxies()`. RemoteIPHeaders [] string // TrustedPlatform if set to a constant of value gin.Platform*, trusts the headers set by // that platform, for example to determine the client IP TrustedPlatform string // MaxMultipartMemory value of 'maxMemory' param that is given to http.Request's ParseMultipartForm // method call. MaxMultipartMemory int64 // ReadHeaderTimeout is the maximum duration allowed for reading the request // headers by the http.Server created through Run, RunTLS and RunListener. // If zero or negative, a default of 10 seconds is used. Set to a positive // value to customize, or use a custom http.Server directly to disable it. ReadHeaderTimeout time . Duration // UseH2C enable h2c support. UseH2C bool // ContextWithFallback enable fallback Context.Deadline(), Context.Done(), Context.Err() and Context.Value() when Context.Request.Context() is not nil. ContextWithFallback bool HTMLRender render . HTMLRender FuncMap template . FuncMap // contains filtered or unexported fields } Fields RouterGroup RedirectTrailingSlash bool RedirectTrailingSlash enables automatic redirection if the current route can't be matched but a handler for the path with (without) the trailing slash exists. For example if /foo/ is requested but a route only exists for /foo, the client is redirected to /foo with http status code 301 for GET requests and 307 for all other request methods. RedirectFixedPath bool RedirectFixedPath if enabled, the router tries to fix the current request path, if no handle is registered for it. First superfluous path elements like ../ or // are removed. Afterwards the router does a case-insensitive lookup of the cleaned path. If a handle can be found for this route, the router makes a redirection to the corrected path with status code 301 for GET requests and 307 for all other request methods. For example /FOO and /..//Foo could be redirected to /foo. RedirectTrailingSlash is independent of this option. HandleMethodNotAllowed bool HandleMethodNotAllowed if enabled, the router checks if another method is allowed for the current route, if the current request can not be routed. If this is the case, the request is answered with 'Method Not Allowed' and HTTP status code 405. If no other Method is allowed, the request is delegated to the NotFound handler. ForwardedByClientIP bool ForwardedByClientIP if enabled, client IP will be parsed from the request's headers that match those stored at (*gin.Engine).RemoteIPHeaders . If no IP was fetched, it falls back to the IP obtained from (*gin.Context).Request.RemoteAddr . AppEngine bool AppEngine was deprecated. Deprecated: USE TrustedPlatform WITH VALUE gin.PlatformGoogleAppEngine INSTEAD #726 #755 If enabled, it will trust some headers starting with 'X-AppEngine...' for better integration with that PaaS. UseRawPath bool UseRawPath if enabled, the url.RawPath will be used to find parameters. The RawPath is only a hint, EscapedPath() should be use instead. ( https://pkg.go.dev/net/url@master#URL ) Only use RawPath if you know what you are doing. UseEscapedPath bool UseEscapedPath if enable, the url.EscapedPath() will be used to find parameters It overrides UseRawPath UnescapePathValues bool UnescapePathValues if true, the path value will be unescaped. If UseRawPath and UseEscapedPath are false (by default), the UnescapePathValues effectively is true, as url.Path gonna be used, which is already unescaped. RemoveExtraSlash bool RemoveExtraSlash a parameter can be parsed from the URL even with extra slashes. See the PR #1817 and issue #1644 RemoteIPHeaders []string RemoteIPHeaders list of headers used to obtain the client IP when (*gin.Engine).ForwardedByClientIP is true and (*gin.Context).Request.RemoteAddr is matched by at least one of the network origins of list defined by (*gin.Engine).SetTrustedProxies() . Copy type StructValidator interface { // ValidateStruct can receive any kind of type and it should never panic, even if the configuration is not right. // If the received type is a slice|array, the validation should be performed travel on every element. // If the received type is not a struct or slice|array, any validation should be skipped and nil must be returned. // If the received type is a struct or pointer to a struct, the validation should be performed. // If the struct is not valid or the validation itself fails, a descriptive error should be returned. // Otherwise nil must be returned. Engine () any } Methods ValidateStruct func(any) error ValidateStruct can receive any kind of type and it should never panic, even if the configuration is not right. If the received type is a slice|array, the validation should be performed travel on every element. If the received type is not a struct or slice|array, any validation should be skipped and nil must be returned. If the received type is a struct or pointer to a struct, the validation should be performed. If the struct is not valid or the validation itself fails, a descriptive error should be returned. Otherwise nil must be returned. Engine func() any Engine returns the underlying validator engine which powers the StructValidator implementation.

Copy type Encoder interface { // SetEscapeHTML specifies whether problematic HTML characters // should be escaped inside JSON quoted strings. // The default behavior is to escape &#x26;, &#x3C;, and > to \u0026, \u003c, and \u003e // to avoid certain safety problems that can arise when embedding JSON in HTML. // // In non-HTML settings where the escaping interferes with the readability // of the output, SetEscapeHTML(false) disables this behavior. The default behavior is to escape &, to \u0026, \u003c, and \u003e to avoid certain safety problems that can arise when embedding JSON in HTML. In non-HTML settings where the escaping interferes with the readability of the output, SetEscapeHTML(false) disables this behavior. Encode func(v any) error Encode writes the JSON encoding of v to the stream, followed by a newline character. See the documentation for Marshal for details about the conversion of Go values to JSON.
